speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of your chronic cough, weight loss, and weakness, can you tell me if you have experienced any fevers, night sweats, or coughed up any blood recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 68-year-old male. The patient reports having a fever, cough, weakness, night sweats, and poor appetite persisting for 6 months. He has lost 7.5 kg (16.5 lb) over this period. No history of breathlessness, nasal discharge, nasal obstruction, palpitations, chest pain, or digestive symptoms. Released from prison 9 months ago after a 2-year sentence.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent release from prison and these symptoms, I need to check for tuberculosis; could you describe the nature of your cough, such as whether it is productive or dry? I will also need to review your medical history for any prior exposure to TB or other respiratory conditions.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Chronic cough and fever. I also have Weight loss, Night sweats, Generalized weakness, Poor appetite.

speaker: Doctor
text:

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal sputum culture makes typical tuberculosis less likely, so I need to explore other possibilities like fungal infections or malignancy. Have you traveled to any specific regions recently, or do you have a history of heavy smoking or alcohol use?
